intro.text: Asset integrity management is the coordinated discipline of keeping industrial equipment safe, functional and suitable for service throughout its life. It connects design information, operating conditions, inspection evidence, corrosion knowledge and engineering assessment so that asset decisions are defensible rather than reactive.

sections.heading: What asset integrity management is designed to achieve

content.text: The central objective is containment and structural or functional performance under defined operating conditions. A credible programme protects people and the environment while supporting regulatory obligations, production availability and lifecycle value. It does not promise that equipment will never deteriorate; it provides the controls needed to identify credible degradation, understand its significance and act before risk becomes unacceptable. The technical basis should identify the affected equipment, assumptions, uncertainties, responsible authority and evidence required to close the resulting action.

intro.text: For static equipment integrity, this category addresses the integrity of pressure vessels, boilers, columns, reactors, exchangers, drums, separators, heaters, air coolers and associated pressure-retaining systems. These assets may be exposed to internal corrosion, erosion, cracking, creep, fatigue, embrittlement, thermal damage, CUI and process-specific deterioration. Effective inspection must connect the equipment design and materials to the actual service environment and provide sufficient evidence for maintenance, repair or continued-operation decisions.

content.text: For static equipment integrity, the assessment boundary may include vessel shell, heads, welds, nozzles, attachments, internals, linings, insulation and supports. The equipment must be considered as a system because deterioration at supports, connections, internals or protective features can influence the pressure boundary and operating reliability.
For this static equipment integrity scope, Asset identity, materials, design conditions and current service should be verified before the condition is interpreted.

For static equipment integrity, the inspection basis should consider general or local metal loss, cracking, erosion, CUI, fatigue, creep, deformation and process-specific damage. Service chemistry, temperature, pressure, flow, cycling, insulation condition, fabrication history and previous findings determine which mechanisms are credible and where they are most likely to occur.
For this static equipment integrity scope, The review should record both confirmed threats and uncertainties requiring field verification or conservative treatment.

Planning for static equipment integrity should define preparation, isolation, access, internal and external coverage, examination techniques, calibration, location referencing and reporting. The selected methods must be capable of detecting the expected form and orientation of damage rather than being applied as a generic checklist.
For this static equipment integrity scope, Achieved coverage and method limitations must be stated so a completed report is not mistaken for full examination.

Findings from static equipment integrity should be evaluated against API 510, API 579-1/ASME FFS-1 and the applicable construction code, subject to confirmed applicability. Where direct acceptance is not available, validated dimensions and operating loads may support remaining-life or Fitness-for-Service assessment. Uncertainty and unexamined areas should remain visible in the decision.
For this static equipment integrity scope, Engineering conclusions must state assumptions, operating limits, approval authority and reassessment triggers.

The static equipment integrity output should distinguish immediate safeguards, additional examination, monitoring, repair, replacement and continued service. Recommendations require priority, owner, due date and closure evidence. The next inspection date should reflect condition, degradation rate, risk, inspection effectiveness and governing requirements.
For this static equipment integrity scope, Temporary controls and deferrals need formal expiry, monitoring and a permanent-resolution plan.

A structured static equipment integrity programme allows shutdown and maintenance teams to plan work before deterioration becomes an emergency. Traceable data also improves corrosion reviews, RBI reassessment, repair planning and future comparison across similar equipment in UAE and GCC facilities.
For this static equipment integrity scope, Updated records should remain linked to the asset, enabling technical learning and accountable lifecycle decisions.

Within this industrial quality inspection subject, Traceability should connect evidence to the correct item, drawing revision and production stage.

Within this industrial quality inspection subject, Concessions and use-as-is dispositions require the designated technical and contractual authority.

The industrial quality inspection report should distinguish work reviewed, witnessed, accepted by the responsible party, pending, rejected, waived or not presented. Inspection evidence does not replace approvals reserved for the client, authorised inspector, regulator or certification body.
Within this industrial quality inspection subject, Clear status language prevents a visit report from being mistaken for final release.

Records from industrial quality inspection can reveal recurring defects, weak processes, delayed documents and effective controls. Trend review supports future supplier selection, risk-based surveillance, improved specifications and earlier intervention.
Within this industrial quality inspection subject, Lessons should be converted into measurable supplier and project improvements.

public_articles.status: Draft for factual and management review

intro.text: IAIS UAE’s Integrated Service Architecture reflects IAIS UAE’s objective of supporting industrial owners with coordinated inspection, integrity and technical services. The organisation is being positioned around evidence-based decisions, recognised technical frameworks and responsive regional support.

content.text: Industrial operators need inspection information that can be converted into safe, practical maintenance and lifecycle decisions. IAIS UAE aims to connect field evidence, damage knowledge, asset records and engineering review rather than presenting individual methods as isolated activities. This foundation story must be checked against the company’s final licence, organisation and approved website claims before release.

The service architecture covers asset integrity, NDT, static equipment, tube inspection, materials and corrosion, marine and offshore, remote inspection, quality surveillance and technical manpower support. Actual delivery remains subject to licensing, approved scope, competence, equipment, procedures and client requirements. This foundation story must be checked against the company’s final licence, organisation and approved website claims before release.

UAE and GCC facilities operate across oil and gas, power, water, marine, manufacturing, infrastructure and emerging energy sectors. Each sector requires an application-led scope based on equipment, service, credible degradation, access and the decision the client must make. This foundation story must be checked against the company’s final licence, organisation and approved website claims before release.

Codes and standards are applied only where relevant to the asset and contract. Their mention does not represent certification or accreditation. IAIS UAE will publish verified capabilities and avoid unsubstantiated claims about clients, projects or approvals. This foundation story must be checked against the company’s final licence, organisation and approved website claims before release.

Clients can share equipment details, operating conditions, known concerns, records and required outcomes so that an appropriate technical scope can be considered. This foundation story must be checked against the company’s final licence, organisation and approved website claims before release.
